text:
A FICO score is a number from 300 to 850 that most U.S. mortgage and card lenders check. It sums up your credit file using five weighted factors.

- **Payment history (35%)** is the biggest factor. A single 30-day late payment stays on your file for seven years and can cost a clean profile dozens of points.
- **Amounts owed (30%)** depends mostly on your credit utilization ratio, which compares your balances to your limits. Balances above 30% of your limits suggest strain. Single-digit percentages suggest you have room to spare.
- **Length of history (15%)** rewards old accounts that you keep open.
- **New credit and credit mix (20% combined)** are the last two factors. A burst of hard inquiries makes a borrower look desperate for money.

Many applicants assume their salary counts, but the model never sees income. It sees only behavior. If you put your statements on autopay and rarely apply for new credit, your score climbs steadily as the algorithm forgives older blemishes.
